tip: Negative future stacks -ma then -yacak on the verb: konuşmayacak means will not talk. The -ma is the negative, -yacak the future.
gezdirdiler comes from gezmek (to wander); the added -dir makes it mean show around. Bize evi gezdirdiler = they showed us the house.
The -meli in gelmelisiniz means must or should. Personal endings come after it: gelmelisiniz = you must come.
gideceğimiz is a future participle modifying yer: the place we will go. Turkish puts this whole clause before the noun, with no word like which.
kalkarsak is the if form: aorist kalkar plus -sak. Eğer only flags the condition and can be dropped, kalkarsak still means if we get up.
To report a command, use a verbal noun plus possessive: kalkmamı söyledi means told me to get up, literally said my getting-up.
yatmadan önce means before going to bed: verb plus -madan önce is the before-doing pattern, and the verb stays unconjugated.
For a reported statement Turkish nominalizes: olduğunu söyledi means said that it was. The inner subject filmin takes genitive -in.
Unreal past condition: olsaydık means if we had been, paired with olmazdı, would not have happened. Both look back on what did not occur.
yapmam lazım means I need to prepare: verbal noun yapma plus possessive -m plus lazım. Swap the ending for who: yapman lazım is you need to.
bitiremedi means could not finish: the -eme inside marks inability, unlike plain bitirmedi, which just means did not finish.
katılmak takes the dative: you attend to something, so it is toplantıya, not toplantıyı, before katılmayacağım.
yağdığında means when it snowed: verb plus -dığında builds a when clause. Kar yağdığında sets the time for the main verb.
ettirdim means I had it done, the causative of ettim. The person doing the work takes dative: tamirciye, to the mechanic.
ısınınca means once it warmed up: verb plus -ınca marks as soon as or when, linking the two events in time.
çalıştığım means the one I work at: -dığım turns the verb into a modifier placed before şirket, with no separate word like that.
konuşuyor olacağım means I will be speaking: present -yor plus olacağım gives an ongoing future action, not a one-time will speak.
